rationale: The latest race data confirms that the candidate with base_speed 0.8, kp 4, kd 1, and ki 2.0 performs excellently on the oval and s-bend tracks but still fails to complete the slalom track, going off track early with high steering oscillation and rms error. The slalom track requires very precise and stable control due to its sharp turns. The feedback suggests further reducing base_speed if slalom completion still fails, and softening PID gains if steering oscillation remains high. Given the persistent failure on the slalom, I will reduce base_speed further to 0.75 to improve stability and control in tight curves. I will also reduce kp to 3.5 and kd to 0.8 to soften steering response and reduce oscillations. I will increase ki to 2.5 to enhance steady-state error correction, aiming to lower rms error on curves and improve line tracking precision. The geometry and sensor layout remain unchanged as they have proven stable and well balanced. The line loss strategy remains 'last_direction' to maintain effective recovery. I continue to request the full set of observations to monitor completion, progress, errors, line loss, and control metrics. I expect these changes to improve slalom completion by prioritizing stability and precision over speed, reducing overshoot and steering oscillations, and improving line tracking accuracy.
